question: Why are antacids routinely given as a pre-medication before obstetric surgery?

options.A: To neutralize gastric acid and prevent aspiration pneumonitis
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure safely before the incision
options.C: To speed up the overall recovery time from general anesthesia
options.D: To completely stop all uterine contractions during the operation

explanation: Pregnant women have a higher risk of stomach contents entering their lungs, so antacids protect them by neutralizing stomach acid. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T2#BMP120_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is considered the single most important action to stop hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Wearing sterile boots
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Routine floor mopping
options.D: Daily linen changes

explanation: Frequent and correct handwashing or using alcohol rub removes surface germs from the skin, greatly lowering cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h3)

question: What blood test result is a classic sign of a pertussis infection?

options.A: Anemia
options.B: Thrombocytopenia
options.C: Eosinophilia
options.D: Lymphocytosis

explanation: Pertussis causes a clear increase in a specific type of white blood cells called lymphocytes. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T5#BMP222_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why does the ICM set international standards for midwifery education and practice?

options.A: To collect membership dues from registered practitioners
options.B: To replace local ministry of health laws entirely
options.C: To prevent doctors from working in maternity wards
options.D: To unify midwives worldwide under a shared professional vision

explanation: Global standards give midwives across different countries and cultures a common purpose and unified professional identity. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h1)

question: By the sixth postnatal week, where should the uterine fundus normally be located?

options.A: Not palpable abdominally
options.B: Level with the maternal umbilicus
options.C: Pressed tightly against the ribcage
options.D: Halfway between symphysis and umbilicus

explanation: By six weeks, the uterus has returned to its normal non-pregnant size and dropped back down into the true pelvis. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T2#BMP227_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which age group is most frequently affected by acute hematogenous osteomyelitis?

options.A: Healthy young adult athletes
options.B: Elderly individuals living in urban areas
options.C: Middle-aged office workers
options.D: Growing children and adolescents

explanation: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis frequently targets the active growth areas of long bones in growing children. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T4#BMP216_U3_T4_h3)

question: How does chronic lack of sleep negatively impact a woman's physical recovery after childbirth?

options.A: It impairs immune function and slows down tissue healing
options.B: It accelerates the natural loss of red blood cells
options.C: It causes the breast milk supply to turn into colostrum
options.D: It permanently prevents the uterus from contracting at all

explanation: Rest is essential for cellular repair; continuous sleep deprivation weakens the body's defense mechanisms and delays recovery from delivery wounds. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a clinical risk of giving an inappropriate fluid tonicity to a patient?

options.A: Severe fluid imbalance within the vascular and cellular compartments
options.B: Immediate strengthening of the cell walls across all body tissues
options.C: Dangerous swelling and rupture of circulating red blood cells
options.D: Excessive shrinkage of cells due to fluid loss into surrounding spaces

explanation: Giving incorrect IV fluid tonicity causes cell damage like hemolysis or crenation, not strengthening. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T4#BMP111_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which large blood vessels collect all deoxygenated systemic blood before it enters the right atrium?

options.A: Right and left pulmonary veins
options.B: Jugular and carotid arteries
options.C: Superior and inferior vena cava
options.D: Ascending and descending aorta

explanation: The superior and inferior vena cava are the two major veins that return all deoxygenated blood from the body back to the right atrium of the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T17#BMP111_U5_T17_h4)

question: Why is the postnatal period a high-risk time for women with substance use disorders?

options.A: Breastmilk neutralizes any remaining drugs in the mother's body
options.B: Postnatal clinics never allow women with a history of drug use to attend
options.C: Exhaustion and newborn demands can trigger a relapse
options.D: Hormones immediately erase all past memories of addiction

explanation: The physical and emotional stress of caring for a newborn on little sleep can overwhelm coping skills and raise relapse risk. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T8#BMP223_U3_T8_h8)

question: Why is keeping vaccines cold so challenging for midwives working in rural Nigerian primary health clinics?

options.A: Vaccines manufactured in Nigeria require freezing instead of cooling
options.B: Frequent electricity cuts and high ambient tropical temperatures
options.C: Rural health posts are forbidden from using modern refrigerators
options.D: Mothers refuse to bring babies to clinics with cold storage

explanation: Hot weather combined with unreliable power supply puts constant pressure on storage equipment to keep vaccines cold. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is it called when the lower chest wall pulls inward as a child breathes in?

options.A: Chest indrawing
options.B: Paradoxical pulse
options.C: Barrel chest
options.D: Intercostal bulging

explanation: Chest indrawing happens when the muscles pull the soft tissues of the lower chest inward because the lungs require extra effort to inflate. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T10#BMP222_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of giving tocolytic drugs during preterm labor?

options.A: To lower the mother's blood pressure
options.B: To slow down or stop uterine contractions for a short time
options.C: To cure any underlying bacterial infection
options.D: To help the baby's lungs grow rapidly

explanation: Tocolytics relax the womb muscle, buying important time—usually about 48 hours—to transfer the mother or give medications for lung maturity. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h6)

question: What physical sign creates the classic thick 'bull neck' appearance in severe diphtheria?

options.A: Fatty deposits accumulating under the skin folds
options.B: Swollen neck lymph nodes and soft tissue swelling
options.C: Enlargement of the thyroid gland in the front
options.D: Severe spasm of the muscles of the jaw and neck

explanation: Massive swelling of the lymph nodes in the neck along with tissue fluid creates the thick appearance known as a bull neck. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T6#BMP222_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of poorly controlled gestational diabetes?

options.A: Neonatal polycythemia and hyperbilirubinemia
options.B: Permanent structural kidney agenesis in the infant
options.C: Neonatal hypoglycemia shortly after delivery
options.D: Polyhydramnios due to increased fetal urination

explanation: Gestational diabetes mainly causes growth and metabolic issues like extra birth weight and low blood sugar after birth, rather than congenital organ defects formed early in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T2#BMP221_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which location of a fibroid causes heavy, long periods because it sits right under the inner lining of the uterus?

options.A: Submucosal
options.B: Pedunculated
options.C: Intramural
options.D: Subserosal

explanation: Submucosal fibroids sit directly beneath the inner lining of the uterus. They distort the uterine cavity, which increases the bleeding area and causes heavy periods. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T6#BMP310_U3_T6_h1)

question: A TBA identifies a woman experiencing prolonged, obstructed labor in a remote village. What action demonstrates a successful PHC linkage?

options.A: Waiting until the next scheduled immunization outreach day to ask for help
options.B: Keeping the woman at home while trying local herbs to speed up contractions
options.C: Telling the family to manage the transport logistics entirely on their own
options.D: Using a pre-arranged referral pathway to send her quickly to the local health center

explanation: A functional linkage ensures immediate, organized transfer of emergency cases to prevent delays that cost maternal lives. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T2#BMP215_U3_T2_h4)

question: Within how many hours should a healthy newborn normally pass their first urine and stool (meconium)?

options.A: 72 to 96 hours
options.B: 6 to 12 hours
options.C: 24 to 48 hours
options.D: After one full week

explanation: Most healthy newborns pass urine and their first dark stool within the first day or two of life. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is it helpful to know the difference between an endogenous infection and a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?

options.A: Only sexually transmitted infections can cause visible changes in vaginal discharge
options.B: Only STIs cause symptoms that result in psychological distress for the patient
options.C: Endogenous infections are always permanent while STIs can be easily cured
options.D: Endogenous infections do not typically require routine partner treatment like STIs do

explanation: Knowing an infection is endogenous saves the patient from unnecessary blame or partner tracing, since these issues come from internal balance shifts rather than outside transmission. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the standard route of administration for a dose of Syntometrine?

options.A: Rectal suppository capsule
options.B: Sublingual absorption tablet
options.C: Intramuscular injection
options.D: Intravenous infusion drip

explanation: Syntometrine is normally given as a single intramuscular injection to provide a steady and safe absorption rate. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T3#BMP213_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care right after a VVF repair surgery?

options.A: Encouraging early ambulation within two hours
options.B: Keeping the urinary bladder continuously drained
options.C: Removing the indwelling catheter by the first morning
options.D: Administering strong laxatives to prevent straining

explanation: Keeping the bladder empty stops urine from building up and putting pressure on the fresh stitches, giving the wound time to heal. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T10#BMP310_U3_T10_h5)

question: What does the timing hypothesis suggest about starting hormone replacement therapy for heart health?

options.A: It should always be delayed until a woman is past seventy years old
options.B: It is safer and more beneficial when started close to menopause onset
options.C: It is completely risk-free regardless of the client's current age
options.D: It has no impact whatsoever on blood vessels or heart function

explanation: Starting hormone therapy early in menopause helps protect healthy blood vessels, whereas starting much later carries higher risks. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T6#BMP320_U1_T6_h3)

question: How does conducting an antenatal assessment inside a pregnant woman's home help the midwife?

options.A: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing during pregnancy
options.B: It allows the midwife to inspect living conditions and practical support systems
options.C: It guarantees that the baby will present in a vertex position
options.D: It completely eliminates all risks of developing eclampsia later

explanation: Home visits give a clear picture of the environment, family support, and potential challenges the woman might face during labour. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T2#BMP316_U1_T2_h3)

question: How should a midwife respond when community members express fear or spread rumors about a health campaign?

options.A: Call the police to arrest individuals who are spreading false information
options.B: Cancel the campaign immediately and pack up all equipment
options.C: Threaten to withhold all future medical care from those who refuse to listen
options.D: Listen patiently and address concerns with respectful dialogue and trusted local champions

explanation: Patient engagement and using trusted community voices help dispel rumors much faster than anger or force. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T1#BMP227_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main energy pathway used by healthy heart muscle tissue?

options.A: Lactic acid fermentation
options.B: Aerobic respiration
options.C: Direct creatine breakdown
options.D: Anaerobic glycolysis

explanation: Heart muscle cells rely almost exclusively on oxygen-dependent pathways to generate the steady energy needed for constant beating. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is it necessary to look for persistent failure rather than a single late skill when assessing delays?

options.A: Single late skills always mean a permanent neurological problem
options.B: Milestone charts are only useful for research purposes
options.C: Babies never change their skill levels after twelve months
options.D: Children naturally develop at slightly different individual paces

explanation: Minor timing differences are normal because healthy children can reach specific targets slightly earlier or later than average. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T4#BMP222_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to routine immunization uptake in Nigeria?

options.A: Misinformation regarding vaccine safety and religious beliefs
options.B: Excessive availability of well-equipped health posts in remote areas
options.C: Geographical distance and difficult terrain to reach clinics
options.D: Fear of adverse reactions such as mild fever or swelling

explanation: A lack of nearby, well-equipped health facilities is a barrier, not an excess of them. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T3#BMP117_U3_T3_h7)

question: A midwife wants to talk to busy traders about antenatal care. Where is the best place to find them?

options.A: Writing a journal article
options.B: Market square outreach
options.C: Conducting surgery training
options.D: Ordering laboratory reagents

explanation: Going straight to busy trading spots lets the midwife meet many women where they already gather. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of the cytotrophoblast during the invasion phase?

options.A: It acts as a physical barrier to prevent any maternal blood from entering.
options.B: It forms the umbilical cord vessels before embryonic circulation starts.
options.C: It produces large amounts of progesterone to maintain the corpus luteum.
options.D: It continuously divides to feed cells into the growing syncytiotrophoblast layer.

explanation: The cytotrophoblast acts as a cell factory, constantly dividing to supply new cells to the outer syncytiotrophoblast layer. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T4#BMP210_U4_T4_h3)

question: What are the two main ways nurses and midwives share clinical information in practice?

options.A: Written documentation and verbal reporting
options.B: Text messaging and email bulletins
options.C: Physician orders and laboratory requests
options.D: Public announcements and private memos

explanation: Clinical communication relies on documenting care in written records and communicating updates verbally during handovers to ensure safe continuity of care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T4#BMP110_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which clinical action should be performed immediately after drawing blood cultures in a septic patient?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with oral medications
options.B: Administering broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Waiting forty-eight hours for laboratory results
options.D: Performing an immediate diagnostic ultrasound scan

explanation: Prompt administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics is vital to control spreading infection and prevent septic shock. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T5#BMP221_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which body system uses chemical messengers (hormones) sent through the bloodstream to cause slow, long-lasting changes?

options.A: The endocrine system
options.B: The respiratory system
options.C: The nervous system
options.D: The lymphatic system

explanation: Hormones are released by endocrine glands and travel through the blood to target organs. This creates a slower, longer-lasting response compared to fast nerve impulses. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T6#BMP210_U2_T6_h1)

question: A client requests an injectable contraceptive. Why is recording her weight and calculating BMI part of the assessment?

options.A: To establish a baseline for tracking potential weight changes during use
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of local anesthetic required
options.C: To diagnose whether the client has an active urinary tract infection
options.D: To determine the correct surgical blade size for implant insertion

explanation: Some progestin-only methods are associated with weight fluctuations, making baseline measurements useful for long-term monitoring. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T2#BMP224_U2_T2_h5)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if the cuff used is too small for the patient's arm?

options.A: It results in a completely inaccurate, falsely low reading
options.B: It prevents the Korotkoff sounds from being heard at all
options.C: It produces a falsely high blood pressure reading
options.D: It causes the patient's actual blood pressure to drop

explanation: A narrow cuff requires more pressure to compress the underlying artery, resulting in an artificially elevated measurement on the gauge. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T20#BMP111_U5_T20_h5)

question: Why is damage to mature nervous tissue a major concern?

options.A: It has a very limited capacity to heal or regrow
options.B: It stops the production of red blood cells
options.C: It immediately destroys the entire peripheral system
options.D: It bleeds excessively when injured

explanation: Nerve cells typically do not divide once fully developed, meaning severe injuries to the brain or spinal cord are often permanent. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful counseling technique when talking to an anxious breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Celebrating small milestones like a successful single feed
options.B: Involving supportive family members in the care plan
options.C: Using active listening and validating her emotional experiences
options.D: Criticizing her technique harshly to force immediate behavioral change

explanation: Harsh criticism only hurts confidence and increases stress; mothers need empathy and gentle guidance. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h7)

question: A 15-year-old boy needs extra building blocks for growing muscles and blood volume. Which dietary component should be prioritized alongside complex carbohydrates?

options.A: Strict fluid restriction
options.B: Adequate protein sources
options.C: Pure refined table sugar
options.D: High amounts of caffeine

explanation: Proteins supply the essential amino acids needed to build new lean tissue, enzymes, and blood components during growth spurts. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which deficiency is most commonly linked to tiredness and poor school performance in children?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Potassium

explanation: Iron deficiency leads to anemia, which reduces oxygen transport to the brain and causes tiredness and poor concentration. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T4#BMP126_U3_T4_h5)

question: A student breaks out with chickenpox blisters during morning assembly. What immediate action should the school health nurse take?

options.A: Send the entire class home immediately for a mandatory two-week holiday
options.B: Ignore the spots until the end of the school day to avoid causing panic
options.C: Administer heavy antibiotics to every child sitting near the affected student
options.D: Place the student in a designated sick bay and arrange for parents to take them home

explanation: Isolating the visibly sick child prevents further exposure while waiting for parental pickup and medical follow-up. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T3#BMP126_U3_T3_h4)

question: A patient completes the screening tool and scores above the cutoff point. What is the most appropriate immediate action for the midwife?

options.A: Immediately discharge her from the maternity clinic to a psychiatric hospital.
options.B: Perform a clinical evaluation and assess for any thoughts of self-harm or harm to the baby.
options.C: Wait until her next scheduled antenatal visit in two months to see if it improves.
options.D: Tell her it is just normal mothercraft stress and send her home without discussion.

explanation: A high screening score requires a supportive follow-up conversation to evaluate safety, explore stressors, and plan appropriate care. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T1#BMP223_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is a major preventative measure against childhood poisoning in the home?

options.A: Transferring bug spray into empty juice bottles
options.B: Throwing expired medicines into open household dustbins
options.C: Keeping traditional herbal mixtures open on the kitchen floor
options.D: Storing chemicals and medications in locked high cabinets

explanation: Keeping toxic substances locked away and out of the sight and reach of crawling infants and toddlers stops most accidental ingestions. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of using LAM as a long-term family planning method?

options.A: It completely stops the mother from producing breast milk after month two
options.B: It naturally loses its contraceptive reliability after six months postpartum
options.C: It prevents the infant from receiving any routine childhood vaccinations
options.D: It requires expensive hormonal injections to maintain its effectiveness

explanation: LAM is strictly a temporary method valid only for the first six months after childbirth, after which other methods must be introduced. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T5#BMP224_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does generalized anxiety differ from clinical depression in the perinatal period?

options.A: GAD has no physical symptoms at all, unlike depression
options.B: Depression only occurs before delivery, while GAD only occurs after delivery
options.C: GAD is primarily driven by excessive worry, whereas depression centers on low mood and anhedonia
options.D: Depression is caused by hormones, while GAD is caused by evil spirits

explanation: The core feature of GAD is persistent, uncontrollable apprehension, whereas depression is defined by profound sadness and loss of pleasure. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T4#BMP223_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why does vaginal bleeding happen when a pregnancy is threatened?

options.A: Partial detachment of the membrane from the uterine wall
options.B: Severe bacterial infection destroying the cervical tissues
options.C: Complete rupture of the amniotic sac inside the cavity
options.D: Rapid hormonal withdrawal causing full shedding of the lining

explanation: When the membranes pull slightly away from the inside of the uterus, tiny blood vessels tear, causing the bleeding you see on the outside. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which type of medication is needed to treat an oral fungal overgrowth like thrush?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Antivirals
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Antifungals

explanation: Thrush is caused by a fungus called Candida, so specific antifungal medicines like nystatin are needed for treatment. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T2#BMP125_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a major danger of giving too much simple salt solution (crystalloid) during severe bleeding?

options.A: Causing a sudden allergic skin rash
options.B: Causing a sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: Diluting clotting factors and making bleeding worse
options.D: Permanently stopping all urine production

explanation: Too much crystalloid fluid dilutes the blood's natural clotting factors, making it harder for the body to stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the most appropriate initial action when a client returns complaining of heavier menstrual bleeding two weeks after copper IUCD insertion?

options.A: Reassure her that this is a common side effect which often improves after a few months
options.B: Immediately remove the device and prescribe oral contraceptive pills instead
options.C: Tell her to stop drinking water for two days to reduce fluid retention
options.D: Perform emergency surgery to repair a suspected uterine perforation

explanation: Heavier bleeding is expected during the first few months with copper IUCDs, and counseling with mild pain relief often reassures the client. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T4#BMP126_U2_T4_h8)

question: A midwife distributes insecticide-treated nets to a pregnant woman attending her first antenatal visit. What level of prevention does this represent?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Giving bed nets stops malaria infection before it starts by preventing mosquito bites, which is primary prevention. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T1#BMP117_U3_T1_h3)

question: What type of vaginal discharge is most typical of trichomoniasis?

options.A: Clear, watery, and completely odorless
options.B: Dark brown, thick, and blood-tinged
options.C: Thick, white, and resembling cottage cheese
options.D: Frothy, yellow-green, and sometimes foul-smelling

explanation: A frothy, yellow-green discharge is a classic sign that helps distinguish trichomoniasis from other common vaginal infections. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T6#BMP116_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary chemical form of energy used by cells in the human body?

options.A: Fatty acid chains
options.B: Glycogen molecules
options.C: Amino acid polymers
options.D: Adenosine triphosphate

explanation: ATP is the main energy currency that cells use to power various metabolic processes and maintain vital functions. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h1)

question: According to safety principles, why do most errors happen in busy maternity units?

options.A: Medical equipment is always too modern for routine use
options.B: Patients refuse to follow instructions during the first stage of labor
options.C: Underlying system vulnerabilities create the conditions for mistakes
options.D: Midwives deliberately choose to ignore hospital guidelines

explanation: Safety science shows that errors stem mostly from flawed systems, equipment failures, or poor staffing rather than pure human negligence alone. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h1)

question: How should a midwife shape their hand when entering the cervix for a manual removal of the placenta?

options.A: Spread out with fingers apart
options.B: Clenched into a hard fist
options.C: Flattened like a paddle
options.D: Formed into a tight cone shape

explanation: Shaping the hand into a cone reduces trauma and helps it slide smoothly through the partially open cervix. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome affect the recipient twin in a monochorionic pregnancy?

options.A: It completely stops the development of the fetal heart and lungs
options.B: It causes fluid overload, high blood pressure, and polyhydramnios
options.C: It causes severe dehydration, low birth weight, and oligohydramnios
options.D: It forces the fetus to turn into an unstable transverse lie

explanation: The recipient twin receives excess blood through shared placental vessels, leading to too much fluid, heart strain, and excess amniotic fluid. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T8#BMP311_U1_T8_h4)

question: Who are some of the key stakeholders to involve during community health mobilization in Nigeria?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.B: Contractors who build federal highways
options.C: Foreign embassy staff living in the capital city
options.D: International tourists visiting the local market

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are respected figures who can help encourage the community to support new health programs. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h5)

question: A patient with a bladder infection has severe lower tummy cramps. Which simple comfort measure can a midwife suggest?

options.A: Applying a warm compress to the lower abdomen
options.B: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to relax muscles
options.C: Placing an ice pack directly over the perineum
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake for several hours

explanation: Applying warmth helps relax muscle tension and eases the dull ache in the lower belly caused by bladder inflammation. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T3#BMP216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice in an integrated primary health care setting?

options.A: Offering family planning during routine postnatal visits
options.B: Establishing clear referral links between community workers and clinics
options.C: Using outreach teams to reach remote communities
options.D: Sending clients to distant tertiary facilities for basic pill refills

explanation: Basic contraceptive supplies like oral pills should be available at the primary care level, making distant referrals unnecessary for routine refills. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T3#BMP224_U1_T3_h3)

question: How does chronic high blood pressure lead to placental abruption?

options.A: It causes the amniotic fluid to increase rapidly inside the sac
options.B: It forces the baby to grow too large for the uterine cavity
options.C: It damages delicate blood vessels supplying the placental bed
options.D: It causes the cervix to dilate prematurely in the second trimester

explanation: High blood pressure stresses the small blood vessels feeding the placenta, making them fragile and prone to rupture. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T3#BMP221_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why are midwives well-positioned to promote mental health in women?

options.A: They have frequent contact with women throughout pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: They manage patients exclusively inside large psychiatric hospitals
options.C: They are the only healthcare workers allowed to give psychiatric drugs
options.D: They receive specialized training in neurosurgery and brain chemistry

explanation: Because midwives see mothers regularly during antenatal and postnatal visits, they have continuous opportunities to observe emotional changes and offer support. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h1)

question: What main physical event starts the process of sinusitis inside the sinus cavity?

options.A: Enlargement of the skull bones
options.B: Blockage of the drainage opening
options.C: Bleeding of the inner lining
options.D: Drying out of all body fluids

explanation: When the tiny drainage opening, or ostium, gets blocked, mucus cannot escape, which sets off the cycle of infection and pressure. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h2)

question: How do strict anaerobes react to oxygen in the air?

options.A: They use it to multiply faster
options.B: They are killed or cannot grow
options.C: They turn it into water
options.D: They are completely unaffected

explanation: Strict anaerobes lack protection against oxygen, meaning exposure to air damages or kills them. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T1#BMP116_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is the partograph particularly valuable in busy healthcare facilities?

options.A: It removes the requirement to monitor the fetal heart rate

question: Which of these is a direct physical sign of swallowing a corrosive chemical?

question: Why is increased dietary fiber and fluid intake important in the care plan for hypothyroidism?

options.D: To help prevent and relieve the chronic constipation caused by slowed digestion

question: What happens inside the breast when milk pressure becomes excessively high during engorgement?

options.B: Blood flow to the nipple increases to maximum capacity
options.C: The milk ducts completely seal shut to stop production

question: Which branch of microbiology studies yeast and molds, which cause conditions like vaginal thrush?

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the relationship between management functions?

question: What is the best way to prevent severe postpartum breast engorgement?

options.D: Initiating early, frequent, and unrestricted feeding

question: Why are corticosteroids generally avoided for long-term maintenance in Crohn's disease?

options.C: They stop working entirely after just three days
options.D: They cause significant long-term adverse side effects

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge a midwife might face when applying the Cairo framework in Nigeria?

question: Which register should a midwife use to record labor progress and delivery outcomes?

question: Why is keeping an indwelling urinary catheter in place important after fistula surgery?

question: Why should midwives avoid heavy medical jargon when explaining examination results to a pregnant woman?

options.D: Patients prefer guessing what their health status is

question: Which body activities does the autonomic nervous system control?

options.A: Conscious thought processes and memory

options.C: Involuntary functions like heart rate
options.D: Voluntary movements of skeletal muscles

explanation: The autonomic nervous system handles automatic body processes without conscious direction. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T4#BMP121_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which phase of simulation is widely regarded as the most critical for actual learning to occur?

options.A: Scenario design

explanation: Debriefing allows students to reflect on their performance, process their emotions, and bridge theory with practice. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T8#BMP312_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why should patients avoid taking dairy or antacids at the same time as oral tetracyclines?

question: What makes testicular cancer different from many other solid tumors in how it responds to treatment?

options.A: Complete resistance to surgical removal
options.B: Total immunity to radiation therapy
options.C: High sensitivity to chemotherapy drugs
options.D: Ability to resolve without any medical care

question: Which two gases are mixed inside an Entonox cylinder?

question: What is the main goal of blood glucose monitoring during pregnancy for diabetic women?

options.A: Maintaining near-normal blood sugar levels without causing severe hypoglycemia

options.C: Predicting the exact birth weight of the baby down to the gram

question: Which teaching method works best for training student midwives to repair an episiotomy before working on real patients?

options.A: A large hall lecture on health history

question: A student completes every procedural step on a checklist for an injection but is rough and ignores the patient. Which tool will most likely catch this issue?

question: How should oxygen be viewed when given to a patient in the hospital?

question: What psychological barrier often hinders cooperation between formal health workers and Traditional Birth Attendants?

question: What does the term wound dehiscence mean in clinical practice?

options.A: The edges of the repaired wound pull apart prematurely

options.C: The suture material dissolves inside the body too early

question: What is the main job of a cervical cerclage?

options.A: To prevent bacteria from traveling up into the amniotic fluid

options.C: To stop all hormone production by the ovaries
options.D: To physically support the weak cervix and keep the pregnancy secure

question: A client notices slippery mucus on Monday, and on Tuesday morning her vulva feels dry and sticky. What does Monday represent?

question: Why do many clients in primary health care settings appreciate the IUCD once it is inserted?

options.C: It dissolves safely inside the body after one year of use

question: How does the measles virus spread from person to person?

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical way the body gets rid of extra pregnancy fluids in the early days after birth?

question: Why are adolescent reproductive health services considered a vital part of family planning scope?

question: Why does a midwife perform a speculum examination carefully during an assessment?

question: What is the primary function of the umbilical vein in fetal circulation?

options.A: Pumping deoxygenated blood away from the fetal heart

question: What event usually signals the start of a potential outbreak in a clinic?

question: What is the main reason for conducting a community diagnosis before starting a new health project?

question: What is the primary target for maternal oxygen saturation when providing supplemental oxygen to a compromised pregnant patient?

question: Why do many advanced COPD patients instinctively breathe out through pursed lips?

question: Why do leftover placental pieces cause ongoing bleeding after an MROP?

question: What is the single most effective action a midwife can take to prevent infections from spreading on the ward?

question: What happens when a pregnant woman takes a systemic cephalosporin?

question: Why does a single syndromic treatment protocol often include a combination of different drugs?

question: Which of these practices should a midwife actively advise women against during vaginal hygiene counseling?

question: Why do progestin-only pills require such strict adherence to the daily schedule compared to combined pills?

question: Why is achieving high vaccination coverage in a community so important for disease control?

question: What condition can a newborn get during vaginal delivery if the mother has an untreated gonococcal or chlamydial infection?

question: Which material is generally NOT recommended for long-term storage of breast milk because chemicals may leach into the liquid over time?

question: How should a midwife test the Moro reflex safely?

options.B: Clap loudly directly against the infant's ear

question: Why do many young girls experience irregular menstrual cycles during the first year or two after menarche?

question: A pregnant patient with past uterine surgeries has trouble with the placenta failing to separate after birth. What is the most likely condition?

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool used during clinical handovers?

question: What are the core areas addressed in a complete, holistic palliative care framework?

question: When do the majority of SGA infants typically experience their catch-up growth phase?

question: Why might a patient with hypothyroidism gain weight even with a poor appetite?

question: Why must a midwife check capillary refill and pulse distal to a suspected fracture site?

question: A traditional birth attendant in a rural village is helping a woman with prolonged labor. What is the best action for the birth attendant to take?

question: What is the best position for a newborn with an open spinal defect (myelomeningocele) during care?

question: Why is it beneficial for adults to choose complex carbohydrates like unrefined grains and beans instead of heavily processed white flour products?

question: A mother says her 10-month-old child refuses to finish a large bowl of thin, watery pap. What practical advice should you give?

question: Why are regular emergency drills important for maternity units?

options.D: They fulfill administrative paperwork requirements for accreditation

question: How does gender inequality directly contribute to the high rates of teenage pregnancy?

options.A: It guarantees that girls receive more inheritance than boys

question: Which common oral antibiotic is usually prescribed to treat bacterial vaginosis?

options.D: Ciprofloxacin

question: Why is late booking for antenatal care a major concern?

options.A: It increases the cost of routine drugs
options.B: It delays essential early screenings and preventive care
options.C: It forces automatic patient referrals
options.D: It stops the baby from growing

question: A midwife notices that many women in a rural clinic miss follow-up visits because their husbands refuse to give transport money. What is the most practical first step for the midwife?

options.A: Charge the women double fees so they learn to demand money from their partners
options.B: Organize community awareness meetings with local leaders to involve men in maternal health
options.C: Advise the women to stop attending antenatal care entirely to avoid domestic conflict
options.D: Report every single husband in the community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Engaging community leaders and male partners directly helps dismantle barriers at the household level and builds local support for women's healthcare. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way for a midwife to support a woman suffering from morning sickness?

options.A: Explaining that the symptoms usually fade by the second trimester

options.C: Validating her feelings and offering gentle reassurance
options.D: Involving her partner or family to help with home chores

explanation: Dismissing a mother's physical experience damages trust and ignores real physiological symptoms; all other options represent supportive, compassionate midwifery care. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is treating only the female patient not enough when managing sexually transmitted reproductive tract infections?

options.A: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn baby
options.B: It leaves the sexual partner untreated, causing reinfection
options.C: It stops the ovaries from producing normal progesterone
options.D: It permanently ruins the effectiveness of future antibiotics

explanation: Without treating partners, the woman faces almost guaranteed reinfection once sexual activity resumes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T3#BMP310_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which clinical finding should prompt a midwife to classify a client's eligibility for DMPA as needing further evaluation?

options.A: Controlled mild hypertension
options.B: Unexplained vaginal bleeding
options.C: Normal adolescent age status
options.D: History of uncomplicated malaria

question: What are the two main qualities that make a research tool trustworthy?

options.A: Sample size and funding
options.B: Data analysis and ethics
options.C: Reliability and validity
options.D: Formatting and length

explanation: Reliability and validity ensure that a research tool measures things consistently and accurately. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is a major consequence when patient data privacy is breached in a maternity unit?

options.A: Antenatal clinic attendance rates automatically double
options.B: The hospital instantly receives more government funding
options.C: Midwives become legally exempt from charting duties
options.D: Patients lose trust and may avoid seeking facility care

explanation: When women fear their private health issues will be exposed, they may stay away from hospitals, risking preventable pregnancy complications. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T2#BMP123_U5_T2_h4)

question: How should a midwife handle traditional postpartum practices encountered in the community?

options.A: Encourage every cultural practice regardless of the health risk
options.B: Condemn all traditional beliefs immediately without listening
options.C: Ignore them completely and pretend they do not exist
options.D: Respect harmless practices while discouraging harmful ones

explanation: Cultural sensitivity is essential; midwives should validate safe traditions while educating families on practices that cause harm, like cord infections from native applications. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why must a midwife identify general danger signs before checking specific symptoms like cough or diarrhea?

options.A: To decide which vaccines should be given on that specific day
options.B: To quickly spot severe cases that need immediate emergency hospital referral
options.C: To complete the administrative paperwork faster for health records
options.D: To determine the exact cost of laboratory investigations required

explanation: Danger signs mean the child is in critical condition and needs urgent transfer before routine assessments are even finished. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T9#BMP222_U2_T9_h4)

question: What element do Traditional Birth Attendants often include in care that formal clinics usually leave out?

options.A: Laboratory blood chemistry analysis machines
options.B: Intravenous fluid resuscitation protocols
options.C: Advanced surgical instruments for caesarean sections
options.D: Spiritual prayers, rituals, and protective items

explanation: Because childbirth is viewed through a spiritual lens in many rural settings, TBAs use local prayers and rituals to address perceived causes of complications. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T1#BMP215_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a primary reason a woman in a patriarchal setting might hesitate to use family planning?

options.A: She lacks any physical transportation to reach the health center
options.B: She prefers traditional herbs over all modern pharmaceutical products
options.C: She fears domestic discord from acting without her husband's permission
options.D: She believes hospitals are only meant for treating severe malaria

explanation: In male-dominated settings, fear of spousal disapproval and domestic conflict is a major barrier to seeking reproductive healthcare. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T4#BMP224_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason that limits food intake in early pregnancy?

options.A: Food aversions
options.B: Heartburn
options.C: Morning sickness
options.D: Excessive bone mineralization

explanation: Bone mineralization is a fetal skeletal process, not a maternal symptom that restricts eating in early pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h5)

question: Which of the following can be used as a temporary emergency splint if standard medical equipment is absent?

options.A: Elastic rubber bands wrapped around bone
options.B: Thin sewing thread wound tightly around the limb
options.C: Plastic rope tied directly against bare skin
options.D: Rolled newspapers or wooden boards

explanation: Items like rolled newspapers, cardboard, or wooden slats work well as temporary splints when properly padded. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T5#BMP110_U7_T5_h6)

question: How many wet diapers per day typically show that an exclusively breastfed infant is getting enough milk?

options.A: Two wet diapers
options.B: Ten to fifteen wet diapers
options.C: At least six wet diapers
options.D: Only one wet diaper

explanation: Six or more pale, wet diapers daily show that the baby is receiving adequate fluid intake from breast milk. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h7)

question: A woman's water breaks spontaneously during active labor. What is the most important monitoring adjustment to make?

options.A: Increase the frequency of maternal temperature checks
options.B: Check maternal blood pressure only once every six hours
options.C: Delay listening to the baby's heartbeat until the pushing stage begins
options.D: Stop recording maternal pulse and focus entirely on contractions

explanation: Ruptured membranes mean a higher chance of infection, so checking the mother's temperature more often allows you to spot early signs of chorioamnionitis. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T5#BMP212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is getting a viral infection in early pregnancy often more dangerous for the baby than later on?

options.A: Maternal antibodies are completely absent early on
options.B: Fetal liver enzymes neutralize viruses poorly at term
options.C: Organogenesis happens during the first trimester
options.D: The placenta is fully permeable only in early pregnancy

explanation: The first trimester is when the baby's vital organs are actively forming. Because cells are dividing rapidly to build these organs, viral disruption during this time causes more severe structural damage. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T5#BMP116_U4_T5_h1)

question: A non-pregnant woman taking ciprofloxacin mentions she also takes a daily multi-vitamin with iron and calcium. What advice should the midwife give?

options.A: Take the vitamin only at bedtime while doubling the evening antibiotic dose.
options.B: Crush both tablets together in water to enhance rapid gastrointestinal absorption.
options.C: Stop taking the antibiotic immediately because vitamins deactivate all pills.
options.D: Separate the vitamin and antibiotic doses by at least two hours to prevent chelation.

explanation: Minerals like iron and calcium bind to fluoroquinolones in the gut and prevent proper absorption, so spacing them out is essential. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T7#BMP124_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why is the exact day symptoms start important when assessing a baby with red eyes?

options.A: Hospitals require this data for routine nutritional tracking
options.B: It determines the baby's exact birth weight category
options.C: Late onset proves the infection was acquired from visitors
options.D: Different causative organisms have characteristic incubation periods

explanation: Knowing when symptoms began helps point to the specific germ, such as gonococcus for early onset and chlamydia for later onset. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T2#BMP220_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary age range for using a Stage 1 starter infant formula?

options.A: One year to three years
options.B: Six months to one year
options.C: Any age after weaning
options.D: Birth to six months

explanation: Stage 1 formulas are specifically formulated to meet all nutritional needs of a newborn up to six months old. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T8#BMP214_U3_T8_h3)

question: How is spermatogenesis different from oogenesis in its final outcome?

options.A: Spermatogenesis produces four equal-sized functional sperm cells
options.B: Spermatogenesis creates polar bodies that absorb nutrients
options.C: Spermatogenesis stops completely in middle age
options.D: Spermatogenesis pauses for many years

explanation: While female cell division makes one large egg and tiny polar bodies, male cell division splits the cytoplasm evenly to make four working sperm. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which community mobilization technique uses local storytelling and performance?

options.A: Private hospital audits
options.B: Laboratory blood screenings
options.C: Rigorous clinical autopsies
options.D: Drama and cultural troupes

explanation: Cultural performances grab people's attention and share health messages clearly using familiar languages and styles. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h2)

question: What advice should a midwife give a client regarding when to take her prescribed NSAID for menstrual cramps?

options.A: Take the medication at the very onset of bleeding or right before pain starts
options.B: Wait until the pain becomes unbearable before taking any pill
options.C: Take the medication only after the menstrual period has completely ended
options.D: Take the pills exclusively during the middle of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Taking NSAIDs early prevents prostaglandins from building up and causing severe contractions, making pain control much more effective. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T2#BMP310_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the main job of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

options.A: Suppressing estrogen to maintain milk supply
options.B: Stimulating nerve endings in the infant's mouth
options.C: Contracting myoepithelial cells to eject milk
options.D: Synthesizing proteins inside the alveolar cells

explanation: Oxytocin causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze, pushing milk forward into the ducts. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T1#BMP214_U3_T1_h3)

question: A client receives Sayana Press in the clinic. What angle should the midwife use to insert the needle into the skin?

options.C: 90 degrees
options.D: 180 degrees

question: What is the daily intake amount that defines a macro mineral?

options.A: Less than 50 milligrams daily
options.B: Exceeding 10 grams daily
options.C: Exactly 1 milligram daily
options.D: Exceeding 100 milligrams daily

explanation: Macro minerals are the minerals the body needs in larger amounts every day, specifically anything greater than 100 milligrams. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is a velamentous cord insertion risky when the waters break?

options.A: The exposed vessels lack Wharton's jelly protection and can easily tear

options.C: The umbilical vein will permanently close and stop all blood flow
options.D: The amniotic fluid will turn toxic upon contact with the air

question: What defines a health post within the primary health care structure?

options.A: It is a large facility equipped with major surgical theatres
options.B: It is the most basic unit located closest to rural communities
options.C: It is a mobile laboratory for advanced blood testing
options.D: It is an urban hospital handling complex specialist referrals

question: Why do rapid population growth and high fertility rates directly matter for frontline midwives?

question: What should always accompany a woman being transferred from an outreach site to a hospital?

question: Why do babies undergoing phototherapy often require extra fluid feeds?

options.A: Extra fluids are needed to keep the eye patches moist

options.D: Breast milk stops working once the baby is exposed to blue light

question: Why is finding out when high blood pressure started so important for a pregnant woman?

options.A: To separate long-term blood pressure issues from new pregnancy problems

options.C: To decide which local food the woman should avoid

question: Which situation requires an immediate hospital referral during a community growth monitoring session?

question: What is the main advantage of a pudendal nerve block during an assisted vaginal delivery?

question: What type of receptors respond to norepinephrine?

options.B: Adrenergic receptors

question: Which sign shows that a baby is latching on correctly for breastfeeding?

question: How does a full-term newborn usually react when you gently stroke their upper lip?

question: What is wrong with the common cultural advice that a pregnant woman must 'eat for two' by doubling her portion sizes?

question: Why is maintaining strict confidentiality important in family planning clinics?

question: Why is it urgent to treat a newborn quickly if born to an HBsAg-positive mother?

options.A: Babies infected at birth have a very high risk of chronic disease

options.C: Innate immunity in infants is too weak to clear the virus
options.D: The newborn liver grows rapidly and needs immediate protection

question: What is a key risk when extracting the severed fetal head from the lower uterine segment?

question: What are the main categories covered when checking a child's developmental milestones?

options.D: Dental eruption, hair texture, and nail growth speed

question: Why should a midwife avoid imposing personal moral beliefs on a family planning client?

options.C: Contraceptive methods always fail if the provider disapproves
options.D: Clients have the right to direct their own reproductive lives

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach activity. Which action fits best within the scope of reproductive health services?

question: Why are women sometimes given a tetanus booster shot right after giving birth?

question: What was a major consequence of the medicalization of childbirth in Western history?

options.A: Pregnancy became entirely free of any complications

options.C: Hospitals stopped using surgical instruments entirely
options.D: Traditional midwives gained higher social status

explanation: As doctors took over maternity care, normal labor began to be viewed and managed as an illness or medical event needing intervention. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which blood vessel is the quickest and most practical route for emergency medicine in a newborn delivery suite?

options.C: Peripheral intravenous line in the scalp vein
options.D: Umbilical vein catheter placed in the delivery room

question: A pregnant woman is prescribed calcium carbonate at an antenatal clinic in Lagos. What advice should the midwife give her about taking it?

options.D: Crush the tablet and mix it directly into cold palm oil

question: Which type of connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments because of its parallel collagen bundles?

options.A: Dense irregular connective tissue
options.B: Areolar loose connective tissue
options.C: Reticular connective tissue
options.D: Dense regular connective tissue

question: A preceptor gives a student low marks for an unrelated physical examination skill simply because the student arrived five minutes late. Which bias is this?

question: What is the main feature of psychosis during pregnancy or after birth?

options.A: A temporary fear of childbirth and labor pain
options.B: A sudden memory loss regarding family history
options.C: An intense emotional sadness after delivery
options.D: A complete loss of touch with everyday reality

question: Which of these is NOT an effect of a standard vasectomy?

question: Why must most bacterial specimens be stained before viewing under a standard light microscope?

question: A patient has a thin gray vaginal discharge and a noticeable fishy odor that gets worse after sex. What is the most likely condition?

options.C: Trichomoniasis
options.D: Gonococcal cervicitis

question: What key detail must a midwife teach a mother to write on every container of expressed breast milk?

options.D: The exact date and time of expression

question: Why do patients undergoing DKA treatment often need potassium replacement?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication following a heart attack?

question: Which of the following conditions is a common cause of provider-initiated preterm delivery in Nigeria?

question: Why is a plenary debriefing session essential at the end of small group work?

options.C: It gives the educator an excuse to hand out a surprise written quiz.

explanation: Summarizing findings allows the educator to correct misconceptions and consolidate the learning points for everyone. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h6)

question: A midwife is packing her bag for an anticipated home delivery in a rural settlement. Which medication must she ensure is included to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?

question: What chemical is used in skin and nail scrapings to dissolve cells and reveal fungal elements?

options.A: Potassium hydroxide
options.B: Acetic acid solution
options.C: Normal saline solution
options.D: Hydrogen peroxide

question: Why should a midwife view an emergency referral as a necessary action rather than a failure?

options.A: It allows the midwife to rest while hospital staff take over
options.B: It shows proper clinical judgment when complications exceed home capacity
options.C: It is legally required after every single home delivery
options.D: It proves that home births are completely unsafe for everyone

explanation: Complications can arise unpredictably, and knowing when a situation requires higher-level care is a core skill of a safe midwife. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T5#BMP215_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary antibiotic combination recommended for treating uncomplicated gonorrhea?

options.A: Penicillin and metronidazole
options.B: Ceftriaxone and azithromycin
options.C: Erythromycin and tetracycline
options.D: Amoxicillin and gentamycin

explanation: Standard protocols combine an injectable cephalosporin with an oral macrolide to ensure effective clearance and cover chlamydial coinfection. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which symptom makes a psychiatric referral essential for a postnatal woman?

options.A: Thoughts of harming herself or her baby
options.B: Mild fatigue due to waking up for feeds
options.C: Feeling slightly overwhelmed by visitors
options.D: Occasional crying spells in the evening

explanation: Any form of self-harm ideation or thoughts of harming the infant are psychiatric emergencies requiring specialist care. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the main reason a midwife should identify local leaders before starting a health project?

options.A: To secure their backing so community members feel safe participating

options.C: To report community leaders who break national health laws
options.D: To collect financial donations for the personal use of the clinic

question: What is the primary treatment used for managing choriocarcinoma?

options.B: Radical hysterectomy

options.D: Chemotherapy
